newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares power ahead to new record high.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares power ahead to new record high.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares remained firm on Tuesday as continued good rains in the agriculture-driven country drew in more local and foreign investors onto the bourse.
"Shares continued very firm today because of the rains and low rates on the local money market. We saw a lot of local and foreign buyers on the stock market," a broker said.

The key 57-counter industrial index added 122.07 points to a new record high of 8,483.56, mainly on the back of a 100 cent gain to 3,700 in blue chip conglomerate Delta, and clothing retailer Edgars and tobacco firm Rothmans' 200 cent gains to 3,600 and 4,200 respectively.

Other counters to trade stronger were clothing and furniture seller Tedco, 15 cents up at 975, winemaker Afdis which added 20 cents to 420, newspaper group Zimpapers which put on 25 cents to 2,375 and clothing company Truworth, which was 90 cents firmer at 900.
The only losses of the day were in horticulture group Ariston which shed 150 cents to 2,450 while pharmaceutical manufacturer CAPS were 15 cents down at 385.

Minings continued lifeless because of weak mineral prices on the international market, with a 500 cent drop in gold producer Rio Tinto pushing Zimbabwe's seven-share mining index 46.87 points down to 1,019.44.
